results.name: Gotham underworld slum/Low-Poly Tenement House
results.description:
A versatile, low-poly urban tenement building designed for gritty, atmospheric environments. Inspired by the rain-slicked streets of Gotham, the oppressive architecture of Max Payne, and the neon-drenched corridors of Neo-Noir cinema.

This asset features modular-ready proportions, external AC units, rooftop cisterns, and chaotic electrical wiring—perfect for creating a "lived-in" sense of urban decay and social stratification.

Key Features:

Aesthetic: Gritty, Industrial, Cyberpunk, and Hard-Boiled Noir.

Details: External cabling, rooftop water tanks, recessed balconies, and industrial utility boxes.

Optimization: Low-poly geometry suitable for PC and Mobile game engines (Unreal Engine, Unity, Godot).

Scale: Real-world architectural scale.

results.name: Electric Cabinet / Schaltschrank
results.description:
The open interior of a small electrical distribution cabinet, commonly found in flats or residential settings.

Protection Devices (Top Row): A row of DIN-rail mounted protection devices is visible at the top.
Main Breakers/Fuses: On the left, there are several modular devices which are likely circuit breakers (Sicherungsautomaten) and a main switch or RCD/RCCB (Residual Current Device/Fehlerstrom-Schutzschalter). The main body of these components is white/light grey.

Wiring: Numerous wires are connected to the terminals of these devices.

Busbar/Distribution Block (Orange): In the center, a striking orange component is visible. This is a busbar or distribution block, used to connect and distribute current (often phase wires) from the main incoming supply to the individual circuit breakers.

Wiring and Cable Management: The wires inside the cabinet are grouped and routed, although there is a typical complexity of wiring expected in a functional electrical panel.

results.name: Rusty Electric Meter Box Mounted on a Tree
results.description: 3D photogrammetry model of an old metal electric meter box mounted directly onto a tree trunk with metallic straps. The box is heavily rusted and shows signs of long-term outdoor exposure, with orange and brown corrosion marks across its surface. A clear inspection window reveals an electric meter labeled “Energo-Pro.” The lower section has torn paper labels with Georgian text and faded numbers. The metal surface texture is rough, featuring rust stains, scratches, and peeling paint. The surrounding tree bark, visible straps, and electrical cables add realism to the setup, representing a makeshift installation typical in urban and rural post-Soviet environments. Ideal for realistic street or infrastructure scenes, visual storytelling, or texturing studies. Scanned with iPhone 12 Pro using lidar and iphonescan technology. Reference for realistic urban environment.

results.name: Old Wooden Door on A. Kazbegi Avenue, Tbilisi
results.description: 3D photogrammetry model of an old wooden door set in a weathered concrete wall on A. Kazbegi Avenue in Tbilisi, Georgia. The double door is heavily worn, featuring peeling blue-gray paint, exposed wood, and visible cracks. The surrounding wall shows chipped plaster, exposed bricks, and rough cement patches, reflecting decades of decay typical in post-Soviet urban architecture. Above the doorway, electrical cables run across the facade, adding to the raw street realism. A small street sign in both Georgian and English indicates “A. Kazbegi Ave.” while a number plate “11” is fixed on the left. The surface details—aged paint, corroded textures, and urban wear—make this model ideal for realistic city environment references, heritage visualizations, or architectural studies of old urban infrastructure. Scanned with iPhone 12 Pro using lidar and iphonescan technology. Reference for realistic street urban environment.
